Elena Morales: FYI — noticed ~120 customers didn't get the 'paid' entitlements after plan-upgrade events coming through the marketplace ingestion last night. Looks like upgrades were received but not applied.
Amanda Chen: Ugh. Any error surfacing in reconciliation?
BillingBot: nightly_reconcile_job(2026-02-03): FAILED - apply_entitlements() raised IntegrityError: duplicate_key on entitlement_id 0x4f3a
Josh Patel: I pulled the raw marketplace events. There are upgrade events, but some have missing order_id and a late timestamp:
```
{ "customer_id": "cust_9a3", "event": "plan_change", "new_plan": "pro", "order_id": null, "marketplace_ts": "2026-02-02T23:58:12Z" }
{ "customer_id": "cust_9a3", "event": "billing_charge", "amount": 0, "marketplace_ts": "2026-02-03T00:01:10Z" }
```
Priya Nair: Missing order_id is the red flag. Marketplace sometimes emits order_id later (async). We need to handle late-arriving order IDs + de-dup.
Liam O'Connor: Agreed. Current pipeline assumes event immutability. Out-of-order delivery breaks the entitlement join. We should backfill by matching on (customer_id, marketplace_event_id) and not just order_id.
Amanda Chen: What's the safe backfill plan? We don't want double-entitling or billing mismatches.
Priya Nair: Proposal: 1) run a dry-run backfill that only marks entitlements in a sidetable; 2) verify counts and cross-check with usage and invoices; 3) apply to production with a lock + idempotency guard.
Josh Patel: I wrote a query to find candidate events:
```
-- find plan_change events with null order_id but a follow-up billing event within 10m
SELECT e.customer_id, e.marketplace_event_id, MIN(b.marketplace_ts) as first_bill
FROM marketplace_events e
LEFT JOIN marketplace_events b ON b.customer_id = e.customer_id AND b.event = 'billing_charge' AND b.marketplace_ts > e.marketplace_ts
WHERE e.event = 'plan_change' AND e.order_id IS NULL
GROUP BY e.customer_id, e.marketplace_event_id
HAVING first_bill < e.marketplace_ts + interval '10 minutes';
```
Elena Morales: Good. Can we coordinate with partner ops to request original order IDs for the affected batch? We might be able to avoid heavy backfills if partner can re-emit.
Liam O'Connor: Partner re-emission is best but we need internal fallback. I'll prepare a backfill script that uses marketplace_event_id + timestamp heuristics and idempotent entitlement apply. It will surface a candidate list before making changes.
Amanda Chen: Also add a monitoring alert for 'plan_change with null order_id' - people should know immediately.
BillingBot: alert created: integrations.marketplace.null_order_id_count threshold=5 within 1h -> paging oncall @eng-sre
Priya Nair: Test plan: run backfill against staging with a 2% sample, compare entitlement grants vs invoices, and have finance sign-off. 
Josh Patel: I'll generate a CSV of the 120 affected customers and include Marketplace event JSONs + our reconciler errors. Sending to #finance for quick triage.
Elena Morales: Thanks team. Next steps: (1) Amanda create alert + page rule, (2) Liam prepare idempotent backfill + dry-run, (3) Josh produce CSV + share with finance and partner-ops, (4) Priya coordinate staging test and sign-off. I'll message partner-ops to ask about re-emission window.
Amanda Chen: On it, will update thread when alert is live. :thumbsup:
Liam O'Connor: ETA for dry-run script: EOD today. Will post instructions for the staging run.
Josh Patel: CSV uploaded to drive: https://redwood.app/drive/marketplace-backfill-1782003456.csv (private link)
Priya Nair: Putting a checklist in the PR so reviewers verify: reconciliation counts, idempotency tests, finance sign-off, partner confirmation.
Elena Morales: Great — if partner can re-emit quickly we avoid touching customer entitlements. If not, execute the staged backfill with tight audit logs. I'll follow up with partner-ops now.
